title: Cloud-Native FinOps (OpenCost) & Sustainable Green Computing (Kepler)
summary: Master CNCF OpenCost unit economics, namespace cost allocation, right-sizing CPU/Memory slack, and eBPF-based Kepler pod energy/carbon telemetry.
learningObjectives: Deploy CNCF OpenCost to measure real-time Kubernetes cost allocation by namespace, label, and controller.
Eliminate CPU and memory over-provisioning slack by right-sizing workload requests.
Deploy Kepler (Kubernetes-based Efficient Power Level Exporter) for pod-level energy and carbon footprint visibility.

curriculumModules.title: CNCF OpenCost & Kubernetes Unit Economics
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Shared multi-tenant clusters obscure cloud bills. CNCF OpenCost correlates cloud billing APIs (AWS CUR, Azure Cost, GCP Billing) with Pod CPU/RAM/GPU/PV usage to calculate exact per-service unit costs.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Enforce mandatory cost-center labels (`finops.kubelabs.io/cost-center`) via admission policies and alert on idle cluster slack > 25%.

curriculumModules.title: Green Cloud-Native Computing with Kepler & Carbon-Aware Scheduling
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Kepler uses eBPF performance counters and RAPL (Running Average Power Limit) to attribute joules/watts of hardware power consumption to individual Pods and namespaces.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Shift batch and AI training jobs to low-carbon grid windows and right-size over-provisioned deployments.

labs.title: Deploying CNCF OpenCost & Enforcing FinOps Cost-Center Attribution
labs.scenario: Deploy `opencost` in the `monitoring` namespace and tag `deployment/checkout-service` in `production` with `finops.kubelabs.io/cost-center=commerce-core`.
labs.productionContext: FinOps chargeback and showback require every production workload to carry verified cost-allocation labels.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: opencost
  namespace: monitoring
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: opencost
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: opencost
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: opencost
          image: quay.io/kubecost1/kubecost-cost-model:v1.113.0

steps.title: Tag Production Workload with FinOps Cost Center

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Verify `opencost` is running in `monitoring` and `checkout-service` in `production` has the `finops.kubelabs.io/cost-center` label.

labs.title: Right-Sizing Over-Provisioned Workloads & Deploying Kepler Energy Exporter
labs.scenario: Deployment `reporting-batch` in `production` is grossly over-provisioned with 8 replicas during off-peak hours. Right-size it to 2 replicas and deploy `kepler-exporter` in `monitoring` to track watts/carbon per pod.
labs.productionContext: Right-sizing idle replica slack and monitoring pod-level watts with CNCF Kepler cuts both cloud spend and datacenter carbon emissions.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: kepler-exporter
  namespace: monitoring
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: kepler-exporter
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: kepler-exporter
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: kepler
          image: quay.io/sustainable_computing_io/kepler:v0.7.12

steps.title: Deploy CNCF Kepler Power & Carbon Exporter

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Check `kubectl get deploy reporting-batch -n production` (2/2) and `kubectl get deploy kepler-exporter -n monitoring`.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which CNCF project provides vendor-neutral real-time cost monitoring and showback/chargeback allocation for Kubernetes workloads?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: OpenCost is the CNCF specification and open-source engine for measuring and allocating cloud-native infrastructure and container costs.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does CNCF Kepler estimate the electrical power consumption (in watts/joules) of individual Kubernetes Pods?
options: By reading hardware RAPL/ACPI power meters and attributing energy to container processes using eBPF CPU/GPU performance counters
By counting the number of lines in YAML files
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Kepler combines hardware power sensors (RAPL, NVML for GPUs, ACPI) with eBPF process telemetry to attribute node energy consumption to individual pods.
